title: Ember and Garden
premise: Yara Whitlock, a royal food-taster who secretly sells charms in a city where magic is outlawed, inherits a dying stranger's map to the Ember Garden — the last living heart of a country erased from history by royal decree. Hunted by the Inquisitor General and shadowed by the stranger's vengeful brother, she must gather three keys of memory held in the minds of people who have been made to forget. At the thirteenth moon, Yara opens the door out of the vanished country, but chooses instead to bring its memory back into the world, dissolving the law against magic and taking her place as the garden's keeper.
about_author: Tamsin Okafor is a former botanist turned novelist who writes about plants that remember what people cannot. She lives above a seed library with two cats named after extinct flowers.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet her swallowing poison at court by day and selling memory-charms in the night market by night, establishing her double life and the Edict that outlawed magic. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Stall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A bleeding man collapses at her charm stall, presses a brass map into her hands, and dies whispering 'the garden keeps score.' She flees before the Watch arrives. Emotional beat: terror and unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The map will not open for her; it shows only burning fields. The Inquisitor General's men begin asking about a dead man. Emotional beat: dread as she realizes she cannot give the map back.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Follows
chapters.summary: Dain's POV (introduced). The dead man's brother tracks Yara, believing she stole his sibling's legacy and caused his death. He corners her; they fight, then are interrupted by Inquisitors. Emotional beat: hostile alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Deciphering the map's inscription: the door out of the vanished country of Vessany opens once, at the thirteenth moon turn. Dain reveals Vessany was erased by decree after a magical plague. Emotional beat: reluctant shared purpose.

chapters.title: The First Key Is a Face
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The first key lives in the memory of Yara's own employer, the Queen's chamberlain, whose forgotten past holds Vessany's border. Yara risks her taster's post to reach him. Emotional beat: intimacy and betrayal of trust.

chapters.title: Poison and Proof
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. During a tasting, Yara detects a real assassination attempt meant for the chamberlain, saving him and earning access to his sealed memories. Emotional beat: justice done quietly, outside any court.

chapters.title: The Chamberlain's Country
chapters.summary: Chamberlain Ovid's POV. His suppressed memories surface: he was born in Vessany and helped write its erasure to save his family. He gives Yara the first key and his shame. Emotional beat: grief for complicity.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Net
chapters.summary: Inquisitor General Sarel's POV. Sarel closes the net on Yara, revealing she knows more about the Ember Garden than any servant of the crown should. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — Sarel believes erasure was mercy.

chapters.title: Night Market Burning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Watch burns the night market to flush out the map-holder. Yara loses her stall, her stock, and an old friend who dies covering her escape. Emotional beat: rage and survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: The Second Key Is a Song
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain remembers their mother singing a lullaby that is actually a key-sequence; his grief curdles when he learns his brother died protecting the map, not stealing it. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into loyalty.

chapters.title: River of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Yara and Dain's alternating POV. They travel the Lethe Canal, whose waters eat memories, and nearly lose themselves; Dain saves Yara by anchoring her with his brother's name. Emotional beat: trust forged in mutual vulnerability.

chapters.title: Sarel's Offer
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. Sarel captures them briefly and offers Yara immunity in exchange for the map, claiming the garden's magic caused the plague. Yara refuses. Emotional beat: temptation and moral clarity.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Aided by the underground charm-sellers' network Yara once supplied, they escape through a buried seed vault where pre-erasure plants still grow impossibly. Emotional beat: hope rekindled by living evidence.

chapters.title: The Third Key Is a Grave
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The final key lies in an unmarked grave — their mother's — which the brothers' family kept hidden inside the capital itself. Digging it up means treason. Emotional beat: sacrilege as devotion.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Under the thirteenth moon's approach, they exhume a locket of pressed ember-flowers. Sarel ambushes them; Dain is captured buying Yara time to run. Emotional beat: cost of every step forward.

chapters.title: The Door in the Hedge
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Alone, Yara finds the door: a hedge grown through the palace gardens themselves, hidden in plain sight. The map finally opens. Emotional beat: awe and terrible solitude.

chapters.title: Inside the Ember Garden
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Within, the garden preserves all of Vessany — streets, orchards, the recorded memories of the erased. It offers her restoration of everything lost if she becomes its keeper forever. Emotional beat: the seduction of retreat.

chapters.title: Trade of One Life
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain escapes Sarel's cells with Ovid's help and reaches the garden as Sarel's forces breach the hedge behind him. Emotional beat: desperate race against both army and deadline.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. Confronting Sarel among the ember-trees, Yara refuses both erasure and escape: she shatters the door's frame so the garden pours outward into the world, restoring memory to everyone under the Edict. Sarel, flooded with her own suppressed past, breaks. Emotional beat: catharsis — memory as justice no law can revoke.

chapters.title: After the Edict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Magic is decriminalized; the chamberlain publicly confesses Vessany's erasure; the country exists again as memory even though its borders do not return. Dain plants his mother's locket seeds. Emotional beat: mourning braided with renewal.

chapters.title: Keeper of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Epilogue. Yara reopens her stall openly, selling charms beside the garden's new public gate, teaching children the names of erased things. Final beat: quiet joy — inheritance fulfilled, not hoarded.
